message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of ways you can stay up‑to‑date with the freshest sports headlines:

| Method | What it gives you | How to set it up |
|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| **Sports News Apps** (e.g., ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report) | Push notifications & curated stories tailored to your favorite teams/players | Download from App Store / Google Play → sign in → enable push alerts |
| **RSS Feeds** | Real‑time article titles + links straight into your feed reader | Find “sports” section RSS link on site → add to Feedly, Inoreader, etc. |
| **Twitter Lists** | Live tweet stream from journalists, analysts, team accounts | Create a list → add relevant handles → follow the list |
| **Google Alerts** | Email digests when new articles hit the web | Go to google.com/alerts → type sport keyword → choose frequency |
| **Reddit Subreddits** (`r/sports`, `r/nba`, `r/premierleague`…) | Community discussion + breaking updates | Subscribe via Reddit app/web → turn on notification toggle |
| **News Aggregator Sites** (Apple News, Flipboard, Pocket) | Curated top stories across multiple outlets | Add sports category → customize sources |
| **Official Team Websites/APIs** | Direct press releases & stats | Visit each club’s newsroom → look for RSS/API access |

### Quick Tips

1. **Mix Sources:** Combine one mobile app with a Twitter list so you don’t miss anything—apps give depth while tweets capture instant reactions.
2. **Filter Noise:** Use keywords (“NBA playoffs”, “World Cup qualifiers”) in Google Alerts or RSS filters to keep only what matters.
3. **Set Priorities:** Turn off non‑essential notifications after the first week if they’re too distracting.
4. **Leverage AI Summaries:** Some platforms (like SmartNews or Microsoft Edge’s reading mode) offer short summaries – great for catching up during commutes.

Let me know which method sounds best to you, and I’ll walk through setting it up step-by-step!
